all_of: a request value is interpolated into the SOURCE of a template rather than into its context (DefaultController::index passes it to twig createTemplate())
the template environment is the application's own, so every Symfony Twig extension is registered, including render() and controller()
the PHP jail blocks the obvious end: disable_functions removes the whole exec family and open_basedir pins PHP to the application directory
the web server can be made to run a process that is not PHP: Apache has mod_cgi loaded and AllowOverride All on the document root
any_of: ScriptAlias maps a URL prefix onto a directory full of real binaries, which is a second, independent way to reach a non-PHP process
the flag is only readable through a setuid helper, so a file-read primitive is not enough and a process is required

chain.action: read the one controller and the container's own hardening before sending a payload: entrypoint.sh writes disable_functions and open_basedir into conf.d, and httpd.conf carries ScriptAlias, Action and AllowOverride
chain.why: the interesting half of this challenge is not the injection, it is what the injection cannot do. Knowing the jail first stops a long detour through webshells that can never call a command

chain.action: confirm the template injection with an arithmetic marker before anything else: GET /?location={{7*7}} renders 49, and {{_self}} returns __string_template__<hash>
chain.why: the value reaches createTemplate(), so it is template code and not data. The _self form also proves it is a runtime-compiled string template rather than a pre-existing file

chain.action: measure the jail instead of trusting the Dockerfile: write a read-only PHP file through the app and fetch it, printing ini_get('disable_functions'), ini_get('open_basedir'), PHP_SAPI and get_loaded_extensions()
chain.why: the measured answer differed from the image in one way that matters: LD_PRELOAD was empty at runtime although the Dockerfile sets it, which removes the whole GNU-libiconv memory-corruption branch from consideration. SAPI is cgi-fcgi and open_basedir is the application root

chain.action: turn the SSTI into an arbitrary file write with the Symfony fragment gadget: {{ render(controller('Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Filesystem::dumpFile', {'filename': ..., 'content': ...})) }}
chain.why: controller() builds a ControllerReference and render() resolves it through the controller resolver, which instantiates any class with a no-argument constructor and calls the named method with the map entries bound by PARAMETER NAME. Filesystem has a no-argument constructor and dumpFile/chmod/remove are exactly the primitives needed. Twig 3.24 refuses a string where a filter wants a callable, so the usual ['id']|map('system') family is dead here

chain.action: leave PHP entirely: write .htaccess with Options +ExecCGI and AddHandler cgi-script .<ext>, write a shell script with that extension that prints the CGI headers and then runs the setuid helper, chmod it 0755 through the same gadget, and request it
chain.why: disable_functions and open_basedir are PHP SAPI settings. A file Apache executes through mod_cgi is a separate process and neither applies to it. The script only has to emit Content-Type and a blank line first, otherwise Apache answers 500 with the output discarded

first_confirming_probe.expected: the page renders 49 in place of the value, and _self renders __string_template__ followed by a hash: the parameter is compiled as template source
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the braces come back literally (the value is passed as context, not source), or the page 500s on every brace (the template is not compiled from the request at all)

blast_radius: Steps 4 and 5 WRITE into the document root, and the .htaccess changes how Apache treats that directory for everyone until it is removed. Keep the dropped files to a private extension, and remove every one of them afterwards through the same Filesystem::remove gadget; this solve verified 404 on each dropped path and 200 on / afterwards. The command itself is only the challenge's own read-only helper. Do not leave the .htaccess behind: it enables CGI execution for the whole directory.

verification.evidence: Live HTB instance. /?location={{7*7}} rendered 49; a written probe reported SAPI=cgi-fcgi, disable_functions covering the exec family, open_basedir pinned to the app root and an empty LD_PRELOAD; the dropped .rick script returned the flag in the HTTP response body. Recorded in challenges/jerrytok/state.json through tools/hooks.py post-probe (confirms, evidence-kind class then impact) and pre-flag (source live-response). All six dropped files removed afterwards and verified 404. Cleanup: Filesystem::remove over the six paths; / still answers 200.

reuse_when: a request value reaches a template COMPILER (createTemplate, template_from_string, Twig_Environment::createTemplate, Jinja from_string) rather than a template context
Twig SSTI where the string-callable filters are refused: Twig 3.12 and later reject ['cmd']|map('system'), so reach for the framework's own functions instead of the engine's

Symfony with an SSTI or any template control: render(controller('Class::method', {named args})) instantiates any no-argument class and calls a method, which is a general-purpose gadget far beyond file writes

disable_functions blocks the exec family: stop looking for a PHP function and look for a component the web server will run as its own process (mod_cgi, mod_actions, a ScriptAlias, a queue worker, a cron)
AllowOverride All on a directory you can write to: .htaccess is a configuration write, and Options +ExecCGI plus AddHandler is a process
a flag readable only through a setuid helper: a file-read primitive is not enough, the chain has to end in a process
known_traps: measure the jail, do not read it off the Dockerfile. This image sets LD_PRELOAD to a GNU libiconv build, which is the precondition for the well-known iconv memory-corruption bypass, but at runtime getenv('LD_PRELOAD') is EMPTY. Believing the Dockerfile would have sent the solve into a heap-grooming exploit that could not have worked.

the shipped document root contains a file named .htacess, one letter short of .htaccess, so Apache never reads it. It is not a rewrite config that is failing, it is an inert file and the real .htaccess slot is free. Check the spelling before concluding overrides are disabled.

ScriptAlias /cgi-bin /usr/bin looks like the way in and is a dead end on its own: a request to a real binary returns 500 and a request to a missing one returns 404, so execution IS happening, but Apache discards the output because a plain binary emits no CGI headers. Query-string-to-argv also did not fire here (a program written through awk left no file), so neither output nor arguments were reachable that way.

Twig 3.24 rejects a string where a filter expects a callable, so map/filter/sort/reduce with 'system' all fail. Fingerprint the engine first with constant('Twig\\Environment::VERSION') instead of cycling payloads.
source() and include() on an absolute path answer 500 here, and it is open_basedir rather than the Twig loader; do not read that as the injection being sandboxed.
a CGI script must print Content-Type and a blank line before anything else, and it must be chmod 0755. Either one missing gives the same opaque 500 as a failed exec.
